newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Sharansky demands economic strategy.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Sharansky demands economic strategy.

text.p: Industry and Trade Minister Natan Sharansky demanded on Wednesday Israel's government come up with an overall economic strategy before going ahead with plans to cut spending.

"An overall macroeconomic discussion must take place in the government with the purpose of adopting an overall and consistent economic policy which will include defining economic targets for various periods of time," he said in a statement.

Sharansky said an economic slowdown underscored by an annual gross domestic product growth of two percent -- compared with rates of four to seven percent in recent years -- required the government to come up with "a full package of steps" and not just a budget cut.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government has yet to decide on whether to make further cuts. The 197 billion shekel ($58 billion) 1997 budget already includes a seven billion shekel cut.
Treasury officials believe another of less than one billion shekels may be needed to meet the budget deficit target.
The Bank of Israel has also called for spending cuts to guarantee the government will meet its deficit target for this year of 2.8 percent of GDP.
Sharansky proposed looking into the reasons for an erosion of state revenues and acting to solve the problems rather than a mere treatment of the symptoms stemming from these problems.
"Only after such a process is carried out will it be possible to know whether there is a need to cut the state budget and to determine the depth of the cut," a ministry statement said.
